title: Add regulated workloads landing page + cross-links to Security FAQ and Evidence Pack index
author: Kira Thompson
release_notes: Docs: New Regulated Workloads landing page plus links to Security FAQ and Evidence Pack request flow.
body:
## Summary
Adds a customer-facing “Regulated workloads” landing page intended for the ABM pilot (FinServ + Healthcare) and general inbound. Includes approved copy, deployment-mode mapping (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), and cross-links to:
- Security FAQ (regulated buyers)
- Evidence Pack index + request guidance

Primary goals:
- Provide a single, compliance-safe destination for outbound/ads
- Reduce back-and-forth during first calls by answering common security questions at a high level
- Make it clear when Dedicated vs Private is the right fit for audit logging / SSO / retention / residency requirements

## Screenshots / preview
Netlify preview: https://deploy-preview-421--redwood-docs.netlify.app/regulated-workloads/

## Content notes (claims / guardrails)
- Avoids “HIPAA-ready / HIPAA compliant” and similar certification language.
- Uses “supports” / “can be configured to meet” phrasing where controls are deployment- or contract-dependent.
- Evidence links are not direct downloads; they route to the request flow with confidentiality language.

## Changed areas
- New page: docs/site/pages/regulated-workloads.mdx
- Nav entry under “Security & compliance”
- Cross-link cards: /security/regulated-faq and /security/evidence-pack
- Small copy edits to the existing Security landing page to point to the new regulated page

## Commits (high level)
1) docs: add regulated workloads landing page skeleton + sections
2) docs: add CTA modules and internal link targets
3) docs: revise security wording + add evidence pack request disclaimer
4) chore: update sidebar/nav and run link checker fixes

## Files changed (high level)

- site/components/CallToActionCard.tsx

## QA

## Review conversation (highlights)

### Soojin Lee (PMM) — requested changes
Comment (2025-05-24): “Headline feels too generic. Can we lead with ‘predictable inference for regulated workloads’ + call out Dedicated/Private explicitly? Also, tighten the section headers to match the ABM deck.”
Author response: Updated hero headline/subhead, re-ordered sections to match deck flow (Problem → Deployment options → Controls → Ops/observability → Next steps). Added explicit “Dedicated vs Private” comparison block.

Comment (2025-05-24): “CTA should be ‘Book a security review’ (primary) and ‘Download benchmark methodology’ (secondary).”
Author response: Updated CTA module. Secondary CTA links to existing benchmark methodology doc (not a gated asset).

### Naomi Feldman (Security) — requested changes
Comment (2025-05-25): “We can’t say ‘HIPAA-ready’ or imply we’re a covered entity/BAA by default. Also remove ‘guaranteed data residency’ language; residency is region + contract dependent.”
Author response: Removed HIPAA language entirely; replaced with “PHI-adjacent / regulated data workflows” and added a footnote: “Controls and contractual commitments vary by deployment mode and agreement.” Adjusted residency wording to: “Regional deployment options and residency controls available for Dedicated/Private.”

Comment (2025-05-25): “Evidence pack should not be linked as a direct list of artifacts. Route to request flow and include confidentiality note.”
Author response: Converted evidence links to the request page and added a short ‘How to request security evidence’ block. Added “Do not forward” language and a note that some items require NDA.

### Elliot Price (Docs) — requested changes
Comment (2025-05-26): “This page is close, but we should avoid sales-y absolutes (‘full auditability’, ‘zero data retention’) unless we define scope. Also add anchor links for the controls section and keep sentences shorter.”
Author response: Replaced absolutes with scoped language (“audit logs with configurable sinks/export patterns”, “retention controls configurable by deployment/policy”). Added controls section ToC and anchors, edited for sentence length, and adjusted nav placement.
